env.world: A fixed finite binary potential-outcome schedule \(\theta\in\Theta=\{0,1\}^I\) on \(K\) coordinates \(I=\{0,\dots,K-1\}\), together with a known finite randomization \(p\) whose support is a nonempty finite assignment set \(Z\) with \(p_z>0\) for \(z\in Z\) and \(\sum_{z\in Z}p_z=1\). Assignment \(z\) reveals exactly the restriction \(\theta|_{O_z}\) on an observed coordinate set \(O_z\subseteq I\) and produces the linear score \(X_z(\theta)=v_z^\top\theta\) for a known coefficient vector \(v_z\in\mathbb R^K\). The assignment is the only source of randomness: the schedule is fixed and is not drawn from a superpopulation. The design mean score coefficient is \(c=\sum_zp_zv_z\), the target is \(\tau(\theta)=c^\top\theta\), the variance matrix is \(A=\sum_zp_zv_zv_z^\top-cc^\top\), and the true randomization variance is \(f(\theta)=\theta^\top A\theta=\operatorname{Var}_p\{X_z(\theta)\}\). Assignment probabilities may be arbitrary positive reals.

env.world: A composite blockwise world with two components. (a) A triangular array of blocks: in row \(B\) there are \(B\) blocks \(j=1,\dots,B\) with fixed potential outcomes, whose assignments are the coordinates of one known finite row-\(B\) randomization law on the product carrier of the block assignment sets; that law is an arbitrary finite randomization, and the only independence imposed on it is the assumed independence of the pairs \((X_{Bj},G_{Bj})\) across \(j\). Block \(j\) carries an assignment-random block score \(X_{Bj}\) with design mean \(\tau_{Bj}=\mathbb EX_{Bj}\) and design variance \(\sigma_{Bj}^2=\operatorname{Var}(X_{Bj})\), and an assignment-level bound estimator \(G_{Bj}\) with design mean \(b_{Bj}=\mathbb EG_{Bj}\), all four moments taken under that same row-\(B\) law. Row averages are \(\widehat\tau_B=B^{-1}\sum_jX_{Bj}\), \(\bar\tau_B=B^{-1}\sum_j\tau_{Bj}\), \(V_B=B^{-1}\sum_j\sigma_{Bj}^2\), \(W_B=B^{-1}\sum_jb_{Bj}\) and \(\widehat W_B=B^{-1}\sum_jG_{Bj}\), with limits \(V_B\to V>0\) and (when it exists) \(W_B\to W<\infty\), a uniform score bound \(M\), a nominal level \(\alpha\), the standard normal distribution function \(\Phi\), the critical value \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\) and the studentized interval \(I_B(\alpha)\). (b) Separately, the independent product experiment, whose assignment law is by construction the product of independent component randomizations: deterministic block weights \(a_j\), component scores \(X_j\), component optima \(F_j\) and \(F_{j,r}\), and the product optima \(F_{\mathrm{prod}}\) and \(F_{\mathrm{prod},r}\). Component (b) is a special case of component (a)'s carrier but not conversely: the row law of (a) is never assumed to factorize into per-block laws.
